notes: §1985:XI.4.3.3 SR3: "A RETURN statement may only be used within the range of an output procedure associated with a SORT or MERGE statement for file-name-1." WalkProgram calls GateReleaseReturnRange below 2002, which seeds ProcedureReach.Closure (followGoTo) with the output procedures of SORT and MERGE statements naming the file and reports COBOL7081 for a RETURN outside; it collects only statements at pc >= EntryPc, so a RETURN in the DECLARATIVES is never asked, even where no SORT or MERGE exists (no range at all), and Closure does not follow CALL (§1985:XI.4.4.4 GR10). Probes at 85 (b/c/e): the witness refused COBOL7081 (accepted at 2002); RETURN in an input procedure and in the main line after the SORT refused; RETURN reached by PERFORM from a MERGE output procedure (RETURN INTO, ran 'MMM','ZZZ','AAA'), by GO TO out of the output procedure ('AAA','BBB'), and in a later paragraph of the output section accepted. Defect: a declarative RETURN in a program with no SORT or MERGE compiles and at run time takes AT END silently. Side note: a refused MERGE adds a COBOL7081 on its legal RETURN (known, PB5496). kb/Work PB5572 holds the defect (code read: op-20261114/out-read6/rd-02.json; rerun op-20261114/records-read6/rerun-log.txt).

next.reason: 1985: "A RETURN statement may only be used within the range of an output procedure associated with a SORT or MERGE statement"; 2023: "may be executed only when it is within the range of an output procedure ... If it is executed at any other time, the EC-FLOW-RETURN". 1985 limits where RETURN may be used as a syntax rule. 2023 states only an execution-time rule: RETURN executed outside an output procedure sets EC-FLOW-RETURN.
